podcast.body: Depeche Mode's "Strange Love" was known to have multiple 12-inch mixes, so many that band member Martin Gore couldn't recall the exact number. This exemplifies how acts embraced the 12-inch single format for extended dance versions within the growing alternative scene. "I want to ask Martin Gore of DePesh Mode, how many 12-inch mixes there were of their version of Strange Love? He just shrugged his shoulders and said, I have no bloody idea, mate."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This single from the "Music for the Masses" album became a global hit, contributing significantly to the band's ascent to superstardom. "Singles from that record, Strange Love, Never Let Me Down Again, and Behind the Wheel, were global hits."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
